title: What are microexpressions?
summary: Josh and Chuck explain micro expressions: brief, involuntary facial cues (often under a second) that reveal real emotion and are picked up unconsciously. They cover Paul Ekman's seven universal facial expressions (happiness, sadness, fear, anger, disgust, surprise, contempt), the Facial Action Coding System developed with W.V. Friesen, and limits of facial recognition screening such as a Logan Airport trial reported around 60% accurate. They discuss prosopagnosia (face blindness) and its brain basis in the fusiform gyrus, along with coping tricks. They analyze Ekman's review of Alex Rodriguez's 2009 Katie Couric interview about steroid use, citing a shoulder shrug (guestral slip), unilateral contempt, and micro fear. They close with a blog announcement and a listener mail story about a card reader who claimed a woman was possessed by a gay man's spirit.

segments.title: Intro and cognitive vs. intuitive learning
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode and a theory distinguishing cognitive (book) learning from intuitive learning (unconscious cue-picking, street smarts).

segments.title: Seven universal facial expressions and FACS
segments.summary: Ekman's research found seven universal facial expressions across cultures. Ekman and W.V. Friesen then mapped facial muscles into the Facial Action Coding System, which measures action units and intensity.

segments.title: Facial recognition screening limits
segments.summary: Facial scanning systems are hit-or-miss; a Logan Airport trial was about 60% accurate, not enough for stopping people. Hosts mention a TSA-style screening concept for detecting micro expressions.

segments.title: What micro expressions are
segments.summary: Micro expressions are very fast facial cues, sometimes under a second, picked up unconsciously by most people though few notice them consciously. They can explain gut feelings about someone.

segments.title: Face blindness (prosopagnosia)
segments.summary: Prosopagnosia is a condition where people cannot form or recall visual memories of faces, linked to impairment in the fusiform gyrus; they can still read expressions. Coping strategies include name tags, notes, and family code words.

segments.title: Alex Rodriguez interview micro expression analysis
segments.summary: Ekman reviewed Alex Rodriguez's Katie Couric interview on steroid use and identified a shoulder shrug (guestral slip), unilateral contempt, and micro fear when he denied drug use, plus a head nod while denying. Fear and surprise are often confused, and socially anxious people can be distressed by these cues.

segments.title: Blog announcement
segments.summary: Hosts promote the new stuff you should know blog on the HowStuffWorks site and a companion article on micro expressions.

segments.title: Listener mail: card reader and possession
segments.summary: A listener named Lee describes her daughter repeatedly falling for gay men, and a card reader who said her spirit was possessed by a gay man named Jerome from the 1800s, removing him without ceremony.
